Whoever wrote it has already explored the codebase and put the plan, paths, and context you need into it — take that as your starting point and don't re-derive the overall architecture or re-discover what the brief already covers. # COR-1436: entire experts re-derives the repo ULID it already has

Repo: `cli`. Linear: https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-1436 — read the full ticket, it has the complete trace.

## The problem

`entire experts --repo owner/repo` resolves the repo's ULID by fetching the caller's ENTIRE repo listing from entire-api and linear-scanning it for a matching `full_name`. It already holds that ULID: the cell-resolution step one line earlier resolved it from core and threw it away.

`runExperts` (`cmd/entire/cli/experts_cmd.go`, ~line 214) does two resolutions:

1. **Core, by slug** — `newExpertsAPIClient` → `NewAuthenticatedEntireAPICellClient` (`cmd/entire/cli/api_client.go`, ~66) → `resolveRepoCellTarget` (`cmd/entire/cli/cell_target.go`, ~70) → `resolveProcessingPlacement` → `lookupRepoIndexEntry`, which calls core with `ListReposParams{Filter: fullName}`, picks `Primaries.Processing`, finds it in `Placements[]`, rejects failed/suspended, and dials that cell.
2. **entire-api, by slug again** — `resolveExpertsRepoID` (~404) → `listExpertsAccessibleRepos` (~427) → `GET /api/v1/repos` → linear scan of `repos[]` for a case-insensitive `full_name` match to get `id`.

Step 2 is redundant. `resolveRepoCellTarget`'s own doc says the owner/repo path "delegates to `resolveRepoCellPlacement` ... and **discards the placement id**". And `resolveRepoCellPlacement` (`cell_target.go`, ~291) returns exactly what experts needs:

```go
type repoCellPlacement struct {
	// RepoID is the placement id (coreapi.RepoPlacement.ID), which entire-api
	// uses as its repo_id — verified identical to the id the old
	// mirrors-based lookup used (coreapi.Mirror.MirrorId) for the same placement.
	RepoID string
	// Target is the cell hosting THIS placement.
	Target *auth.CellTarget
}
```

`auth.CellTarget` is only `{BaseURL, Jurisdiction}`, which is why the id is lost between the two steps.

## The fix

**`explain` already does this correctly — copy it.** `cmd/entire/cli/explain_repo.go`, ~line 36 calls `resolveRepoCellPlacement` and uses `placement.RepoID`. Read that first; it is the pattern.

Change `experts` to resolve once:

* For the owner/repo form, call `resolveRepoCellPlacement(ctx, owner, repo)` and use `placement.RepoID` as the repo id and `placement.Target` for the cell client.
* Delete `resolveExpertsRepoID`, `listExpertsAccessibleRepos`, `expertsRepoListItem` and `expertsReposListPath`, plus their tests.
* Keep `expertsAPIPath(repoID)` — the `POST /api/v1/repos/{id}/experts` call is unchanged.
* The ULID form is unaffected: `repoIsULID` already short-circuits resolution and passes the id straight through. Do not change that branch.

You will need the cell client built from the placement's `Target` rather than from `newExpertsAPIClient(ctx, insecureHTTP, fullName, ulid)`. Look at how `explain_repo.go` gets its client from a `repoCellPlacement` and follow it. `newExpertsAPIClient` exists as a test seam (`setExpertsClientFactoryForTest`) — keep a seam of equivalent shape so the existing tests can still substitute a stub, but it may need a different signature now.

**Do NOT re-implement the id-from-placement logic.** The single most important property, from `resolveRepoCellPlacement`'s doc:

> a placement id is only resolvable by the cell hosting that placement ... Taking the id from one placement and routing to a cell chosen some other way asks a cell about an id it has never seen, which comes back as an indistinguishable 404.

Using the `RepoID` and `Target` from the SAME `repoCellPlacement` is exactly what preserves that. Don't split them or re-resolve either half.

While you are there, update `resolveRepoCellPlacement`'s doc comment — it says the placement id is one "which `resolveRepoCellTarget` has no caller for", and that stops being true.

## Behaviour changes to expect (and state in the PR)

**Error messages change, for the better.** Today a miss produces `resolveExpertsRepoID`'s three-guesses message: "repo %q was not found on the entire-api cell this command reached. It may be homed in another Entire region ... not onboarded to Entire, or outside your access". Core's resolution instead distinguishes not-onboarded from a failed/suspended placement and says which. Check `errRepoNotOnboarded` and `renderRepoNotOnboarded` — `runExperts` already handles the not-onboarded render for the client-construction failure, so make sure the same handling still applies now that resolution happens earlier/differently, and that no error gets double-wrapped (`cellPlacementError` and `resolveProcessingPlacement` both deliberately avoid naming the repo twice — read those comments before adding a wrap).

**A latent public-repo bug is fixed.** entire-api's `/repos` is the affiliation set (`repo/list`, which excludes the `public_viewer` wildcard), so today `entire experts --repo owner/repo` on a public repo the caller can read but does not belong to reports "not found" — even though the `POST .../experts` behind it is `repo#pull`-gated and would have succeeded. Core's filtered lookup is scoped to what the caller can read, so routing through it fixes this. This is NOT reproduced — do not claim it as fixed in the PR unless you can show it; describe it as expected.

## Tests

There are existing experts tests (`cmd/entire/cli/experts_cmd_test.go` or similar) using the `setExpertsClientFactoryForTest` seam, and cell-resolution tests around `cell_target.go`. Read both before changing the seam.

Cover:
* The owner/repo form resolves via `resolveRepoCellPlacement` and posts to `/api/v1/repos/{placement.RepoID}/experts` — with NO call to `GET /api/v1/repos`. That absence is the regression guard; assert it, don't just assert the happy path.
* The ULID form still bypasses resolution entirely.
* Not-onboarded and failed/suspended-placement errors surface with their own messages, not double-wrapped.

Delete the tests that covered `resolveExpertsRepoID` / `listExpertsAccessibleRepos` along with the functions.

## Verification

Run the repo's checks — see `Makefile` / `CLAUDE.md` (`go test ./...`, vet/lint). Report honestly what you ran and what passed; if something can't run in the worktree, say so rather than claiming green.

## Deliverable

Commit on the worktree branch and open a PR. Put the handoff in the PR description — do NOT write a HANDOFF.md or any similar summary file into the repo.

The PR description must state: what now resolves the repo id, what was deleted, how the test seam changed, which error messages change and why that is an improvement, and what you tested.

## Context worth knowing

This is the last known caller of entire-api's `GET /repos`, which we want to retire (COR-1370). The other two consumers already moved off it: entire.io's dispatch on 2026-09-01, and mcp's `list_entire_repos` on 2026-09-02. This change stops NEW CLI builds calling it; released versions in the wild will keep calling until they age out, so the endpoint can't be deleted immediately — that's tracked separately, not your concern here.

18	// checkpoint reader tiers the renderers consume, plus the two cross-repo-only
19	// extras (author and anchoring commit) that normally come from local git.
20	// Narrowed to an interface so tests can drive the render paths without a cell.
21	type crossRepoReader interface {
22		checkpoint.CheckpointReader
23		checkpoint.SessionReader
24		GetCheckpointAuthor(ctx context.Context, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) (checkpoint.Author, error)

28	// newCrossRepoReader builds the API-backed reader for owner/repo. Injectable so
29	// tests can substitute a fake cell (see explain_repo_test.go).
30	var newCrossRepoReader = func(ctx context.Context, insecureHTTP bool, owner, repo string) (crossRepoReader, error) {
31		ownerRepo := owner + "/" + repo
32		// Resolve the repo_id and the cell together, from one placement: a mirror id
33		// is only resolvable by the cell holding that placement, so a
34		// separately-chosen cell (the caller's home cell, for a multi-region repo)
35		// would be asked about an id it has never seen and answer 404.
36		placement, err := resolveRepoCellPlacement(ctx, owner, repo)
37		if err != nil {
38			// Not wrapped with ownerRepo: resolveRepoCellPlacement already names it,
39			// and adding it here is what made this path print the repo twice.
40			return nil, err

42		client, err := auth.NewEntireAPICellClient(ctx, insecureHTTP, placement.Target)
43		if err != nil {

45			// errors (login hint, discovery guidance); surface them verbatim.

51	// crossRepoReadKey marks a context as rendering a checkpoint read from another
52	// repo. Context-scoped so the renderers can adjust their guidance without an
53	// extra positional parameter through every formatCheckpointOutput call site.
54	type crossRepoReadKey struct{}
55	
56	// withCrossRepoRead marks ctx as reading ownerRepo's checkpoint from that
57	// repo's cell.
58	func withCrossRepoRead(ctx context.Context, ownerRepo string) context.Context {
59		return context.WithValue(ctx, crossRepoReadKey{}, ownerRepo)
60	}
61	
62	// crossRepoReadSource returns the repo a checkpoint is being read from when the
63	// current render is a cross-repo one.
64	func crossRepoReadSource(ctx context.Context) (string, bool) {

69	// crossRepoExplainOptions carries what `explain --repo` needs to render a
70	// foreign repo's checkpoint.
71	type crossRepoExplainOptions struct {
72		repoFlag string
73		// target is the checkpoint the user asked for, before ID validation.
74		target string
75	
76		json          bool
77		transcript    bool
78		rawTranscript bool
79		// sessionIndex is -1 for "latest session".
80		sessionIndex int
81	
82		verbose bool
83		full    bool
84		noPager bool
85	
86		insecureHTTP bool

89	// parseExplainRepoFlag parses `--repo`. Accepted shapes are `owner/name` and
90	// `gh/owner/name` (leading slash optional), matching the `repo` field of
91	// `entire search` results, which is where a cross-repo checkpoint ID comes
92	// from. Returns lowercased coordinates, as the control plane persists them.
93	//
94	// A bare repo ID is deliberately not accepted: the control plane and the search
95	// index expose different identifiers for a repository, and guessing which space
96	// an opaque ID belongs to would key the cell lookup off the wrong one.
97	func parseExplainRepoFlag(value string) (owner, repo string, err error) {
98		v := strings.TrimSpace(value)
99		if v == "" {
100			return "", "", errors.New("--repo requires a value: owner/name or gh/owner/name")
101		}
102		if !strings.Contains(v, "/") {
103			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("invalid --repo %q: expected owner/name or gh/owner/name", value)
104		}
105		// Normalize to the gh/owner/name clone-ref shape so the mirror parser's
106		// GitHub charset validation applies to both accepted forms.
107		ref := strings.TrimPrefix(v, "/")
108		if !strings.HasPrefix(ref, "gh/") {
109			ref = "gh/" + ref
110		}
111		_, owner, repo, err = parseMirrorCloneRef(ref)
112		if err != nil {
113			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("invalid --repo %q: expected owner/name or gh/owner/name: %w", value, err)
114		}
115		return owner, repo, nil

118	// explainRepoTargetsCurrentRepo reports whether the --repo value names the repo
119	// checked out here. An unparseable value returns false so the cross-repo path
120	// runs and reports the parse error, rather than silently falling through to the
121	// local path.
122	func explainRepoTargetsCurrentRepo(ctx context.Context, repoFlag string) bool {
123		owner, repo, err := parseExplainRepoFlag(repoFlag)
124		if err != nil {
125			return false
126		}
127		return explainRepoIsCurrent(ctx, owner, repo)
128	}
129	
130	// explainRepoIsCurrent reports whether owner/repo names the same repository as
131	// the cwd worktree's origin remote (which handles ssh, https, and entire://
132	// mirror URL forms). --repo is GitHub-scoped, so a non-GitHub origin with a
133	// coincidentally matching owner/name must not match. Best-effort: any lookup or
134	// parse failure returns false and the cross-repo path runs.
135	//
136	// When it does match, explain falls through to the local path — which is both
137	// faster and strictly more capable, since it can read checkpoints that have not
138	// been pushed yet.
139	func explainRepoIsCurrent(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string) bool {
140		curForge, curOwner, curRepo, err := gitremote.ResolveRemoteRepo(ctx, "origin")
141		if err != nil || curForge != "gh" {
142			return false
143		}
144		return strings.EqualFold(curOwner, owner) && strings.EqualFold(curRepo, repo)
145	}
146	
147	// runCrossRepoExplain explains a checkpoint owned by another repository by
148	// reading it from that repo's cell over HTTP. Nothing is written to the local
149	// repository: no ref, no objects, no session state — so a foreign checkpoint
150	// never shows up in this repo's own checkpoint history or token profile.
151	//
152	// The output modes reuse the same renderers as the local path, so a foreign
153	// checkpoint prints identically to a local one.
154	func runCrossRepoExplain(ctx context.Context, w, errW io.Writer, opts crossRepoExplainOptions) error {
155		owner, repoName, err := parseExplainRepoFlag(opts.repoFlag)
156		if err != nil {
157			return err
158		}
159		ownerRepo := owner + "/" + repoName
160	
161		// A prefix can't be resolved without listing the foreign repo's
162		// checkpoints, which is `entire search`'s job, so cross-repo needs the
163		// whole ID.
164		cid, err := id.NewCheckpointID(opts.target)
165		if err != nil {
166			return fmt.Errorf("--repo requires a full checkpoint ID (12-char hex or 26-char ULID); a prefix cannot be resolved in another repo: %w", err)
167		}
168	
169		reader, err := newCrossRepoReader(ctx, opts.insecureHTTP, owner, repoName)
170		if err != nil {
171			if rendered := renderRepoNotOnboarded(errW, ownerRepo, err); rendered != nil {
172				return rendered
173			}
174			return err
175		}
176		// Marked for the renderers: a foreign checkpoint cannot be written to, so
177		// they must not offer actions that only work in the owning repo.
178		ctx = withCrossRepoRead(ctx, ownerRepo)
179	
180		stop := startSpinner(errW, fmt.Sprintf("Reading checkpoint %s from %s", cid, ownerRepo))
181		// Read directly rather than through checkpoint.ReadCheckpoint: the helper
182		// prefixes "read persistent checkpoint:", which buries the reader's
183		// already-user-facing message (e.g. the not-pushed-yet guidance) behind
184		// storage vocabulary that means nothing for a repo read over HTTP.
185		summary, err := reader.Read(ctx, cid)
186		if err != nil {
187			stop(false)
188			return err //nolint:wrapcheck // the reader's errors already name the checkpoint and repo
189		}
190		if summary == nil {
191			stop(false)
192			return fmt.Errorf("checkpoint %s is not available for %s", cid, ownerRepo)
193		}
194	
195		switch {
196		case opts.transcript || opts.rawTranscript:
197			content, contentErr := readCrossRepoSessionContent(ctx, reader, cid, summary, opts.sessionIndex)
198			if contentErr != nil {
199				stop(false)
200				return contentErr
201			}
202			// Every failure has to land before stop(true): an empty transcript is a
203			// failure, and reporting it after a ✓ line tells the reader the read
204			// succeeded and then contradicts it.
205			if len(content.Transcript) == 0 {
206				stop(false)
207				return fmt.Errorf("checkpoint %s in %s has no transcript", cid, ownerRepo)
208			}
209			stop(true)
210			if _, err := w.Write(content.Transcript); err != nil {
211				return fmt.Errorf("failed to write transcript: %w", err)
212			}
213			return nil
214	
215		case opts.json:
216			envelope, failed := buildCheckpointJSONEnvelope(ctx, reader, summary, cid)
217			stop(!envelope.Partial)
218			enc := json.NewEncoder(w)
219			enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
220			if err := enc.Encode(envelope); err != nil {
221				return fmt.Errorf("failed to encode checkpoint json: %w", err)
222			}
223			// Parity with the local --json path: fail hard so automation can't
224			// mistake incomplete metadata for a clean export. The envelope, with
225			// its per-session error fields, is already on stdout.
226			if envelope.Partial {
227				fmt.Fprintf(errW, "checkpoint %s: failed to read metadata for %d session(s) (indexes %v)\n", cid, len(failed), failed)
228				return NewSilentError(fmt.Errorf("checkpoint %s export incomplete: %d session(s) unreadable", cid, len(failed)))
229			}
230			return nil
231	
232		default:
233			content, contentErr := readCrossRepoSessionContent(ctx, reader, cid, summary, opts.sessionIndex)
234			if contentErr != nil {
235				stop(false)
236				return contentErr
237			}
238			author, _ := reader.GetCheckpointAuthor(ctx, cid) //nolint:errcheck // author is optional
239			commits, _ := reader.checkpointCommit(ctx, cid)   //nolint:errcheck // best-effort, already-cached read
240			// Stop before the first write to w so stderr spinner frames never
241			// interleave with stdout content.
242			stop(false)
243			output := formatCheckpointOutput(ctx, summary, content, cid, commits, author, opts.verbose, opts.full, w)
244			outputExplainContent(w, output, opts.noPager)
245			return nil
246		}
247	}
248	
249	// readCrossRepoSessionContent reads the requested session, or the latest when
250	// no explicit index was given.
251	func readCrossRepoSessionContent(ctx context.Context, reader crossRepoReader, cid id.CheckpointID, summary *checkpoint.CheckpointSummary, sessionIndex int) (*checkpoint.SessionContent, error) {
252		if sessionIndex < 0 {
253			content, err := checkpoint.ReadLatestSessionContent(ctx, reader, cid, summary)
254			if err != nil {
255				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read checkpoint content for %s: %w", cid, err)
256			}
257			return content, nil
258		}
259		content, err := reader.ReadSessionContent(ctx, cid, sessionIndex)
260		if err != nil {
261			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read checkpoint content for %s: %w", cid, err)
262		}
263		return content, nil
264	}
265	
266	// crossRepoExplainSessionIndex maps the --session-index flag to the reader's
267	// convention (-1 = latest), so an unset flag reads the latest session.
268	func crossRepoExplainSessionIndex(changed bool, value int) int {
269		if !changed {
270			return -1
271		}
272		return value
273	}
274	
275	// assert the API reader satisfies the read surface the render paths need.
276	var _ crossRepoReader = (*apiCheckpointReader)(nil)

## claude.ai entire-prod-us
Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Reads are curated `*_entire` tools; a small write/ops group covers trail/review/runner/dispatch mutations.

Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

Querying conventions (shared by every tool):
- Addressing: name a repo by a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) or a repo ULID. Repo ULIDs are REGION-SCOPED — the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never carry a ULID across regions or sessions; if a tool rejects one, re-resolve with resolve_entire_repo.
- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".
- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).
- Size: reads that can be large (files, diffs, transcripts) honor max_tokens and return next_cursor to continue — raise max_tokens or page rather than assuming truncation is the whole story.

Pitfalls:
- sessions[].tokenUsage on a checkpoint is a PER-CHECKPOINT delta, not a session total — sum across a session's checkpoints, or use get_entire_session for the authoritative total.
- list_entire_checkpoints silently truncates older history; for a branch's COMPLETE checkpoint membership, paginate list_entire_commits and collect the per-commit checkpoint IDs.

Skills: before deep work in a domain, load the matching skill (list_entire_skills / load_entire_skill) — entire/checkpoints-and-sessions and entire/token-analysis before token accounting, … [truncated]

## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

22	// cell read cannot proceed without: resolveRepoCellTarget (trails, experts)
23	// and resolveRepoCellPlacement (checkpoint/explain --repo).

25	// Deliberately not cellResolveTimeout: that budget bounds *best-effort*
26	// lookups whose failure silently degrades to jurisdiction routing, so it can
27	// be aggressive. Here a timeout is a visible command failure, and the budget
28	// has to cover two sequential control-plane round trips (a repo lookup, then
29	// the cluster catalog), so it is more patient.

32	// so a reachable-but-slow core is otherwise unbounded, and this runs before the
33	// command's spinner starts — the user would sit in front of a silent terminal.

36	// cellCoreClient is the control-plane surface the cell-target resolver needs.
37	// An interface (with a swappable constructor) so the resolver is unit-testable
38	// against a fake control plane; *coreapi.Client satisfies it.

49	// resolveRepoCellTarget resolves the entire-api cell that HOSTS the given
50	// repo, plus that cell's jurisdiction, so a repo-scoped call (trails, experts)
51	// reaches the region that owns the repo — mirroring how the entire.io BFF
52	// selects a cell per repo (list-repos-index.ts' processingPlacement()) rather
53	// than using the caller's home cell.
54	//
55	// This is NOT best-effort: every failure (control-plane error or timeout,
56	// repo not onboarded, no/failed/suspended processing placement, missing
57	// apiUrl) returns a descriptive error instead of falling back to the
58	// caller's home cell. A silent wrong-region "success" is worse than a command

124	// reliable key for a placement — see cell_fanout.go's groupReposByCell), then

263	// repoCellPlacement is a repo's processing placement: the id entire-api keys
264	// repo-scoped routes on, paired with the cell that actually holds it.
265	type repoCellPlacement struct {
266		// RepoID is the placement id (coreapi.RepoPlacement.ID), which entire-api
267		// uses as its repo_id — verified identical to the id the old
268		// mirrors-based lookup used (coreapi.Mirror.MirrorId) for the same
269		// placement.

275	// resolveRepoCellPlacement resolves a GitHub repo to its processing
276	// placement's (repo_id, cell) pair for repo-scoped cell reads.
277	//
278	// The pair must come from the same placement: a placement id is only
279	// resolvable by the cell hosting that placement, and entire-api's data lives
280	// on exactly one placement (the processing one) even when the repo is
281	// mirrored elsewhere too. Taking the id from one placement and routing to a
282	// cell chosen some other way asks a cell about an id it has never seen, which
283	// comes back as an indistinguishable 404.
284	//
285	// resolveRepoCellTarget's owner/repo path delegates to this function and
286	// discards RepoID, rather than the two duplicating the same resolution body:
287	// the two functions exist separately only because their callers need
288	// different return shapes for the same lookup — this one also needs the
289	// placement id (repo_id), which resolveRepoCellTarget has no caller for and
290	// so doesn't return — not because the resolution logic itself differs.
291	func resolveRepoCellPlacement(ctx context.Context, owner, repo string) (repoCellPlacement, error) {
292		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, requiredCellResolveTimeout)
293		defer cancel()
294	
295		c, err := newCellCoreClient()
296		if err != nil {
297			return repoCellPlacement{}, fmt.Errorf("control plane unavailable: %w", err)
298		}
299		fullName := owner + "/" + repo
300		placement, err := resolveProcessingPlacement(ctx, c, fullName)
301		if err != nil {
302			return repoCellPlacement{}, cellPlacementError(ctx, fullName, fmt.Errorf("resolve processing placement for %s: %w", fullName, err))
303		}
304		target, err := cellTargetForPlacement(ctx, c, placement)
305		if err != nil {
306			return repoCellPlacement{}, cellPlacementError(ctx, fullName, fmt.Errorf("resolve cell for %s: %w", fullName, err))
307		}
308		// Trimmed for the same reason the match is: RepoID becomes a path segment
309		// in entire-api URLs, so tolerating a padded id in the lookup without
310		// normalizing it here would trade a loud "not in the placement list" for
311		// a malformed request.
312		return repoCellPlacement{RepoID: strings.TrimSpace(placement.ID), Target: target}, nil
313	}

315	// cellPlacementError reports a timeout as a timeout: without this, a fired
316	// deadline surfaces as whichever "not found"/"no processing placement" error
317	// the caller's lookup happened to return, and the user goes looking for a
318	// missing mirror instead of a slow control plane. subject is the repo the
319	// lookup was for, named however the caller addressed it (owner/repo or ULID).

322	// timeout, and calling it one sends the user hunting a slow control plane that
323	// was never the problem; the cancelled in-flight call's own error already
324	// carries context.Canceled, which is what renderDataAPIAuthError silences on.
325	func cellPlacementError(ctx context.Context, subject string, fallback error) error {
326		if ctxErr := ctx.Err(); errors.Is(ctxErr, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
327			return fmt.Errorf("resolving the Entire cell for %s timed out: %w", subject, ctxErr)
328		}
329		return fallback

332	// isActiveMirror reports whether a mirror placement can currently serve the
333	// repo: not archived, and not in a failed/suspended clone state. An unset status
334	// is treated as active (older data). Shared by every caller that must ignore
335	// placements a cell can't answer for.
336	func isActiveMirror(m coreapi.Mirror) bool {
337		if m.IsArchived.Or(false) {
338			return false
339		}
340		st := m.Status.Or(coreapi.MirrorStatusReady)
341		return st != coreapi.MirrorStatusFailed && st != coreapi.MirrorStatusSuspended
342	}

344	// matchClusterByHost finds the catalog cluster whose public host equals
345	// clusterHost (case-insensitive). The cluster's apiUrl + jurisdiction are the
346	// authoritative cell coordinates. Used by the ULID path (GetRepo returns a
347	// host, not a slug).
348	func matchClusterByHost(clusters []coreapi.Cluster, clusterHost string) (coreapi.Cluster, bool) {
349		want := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(clusterHost))
350		if want == "" {
351			return coreapi.Cluster{}, false
352		}
353		for _, cl := range clusters {
354			host, err := hostFromPublicURL(cl.PublicUrl)
355			if err != nil {
356				continue
357			}
358			if strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimSpace(host), want) {
359				return cl, true
360			}
361		}
362		return coreapi.Cluster{}, false
363	}

366	// (case-insensitive). Used by the owner/repo path: a RepoPlacement carries a
367	// ClusterSlug, not a host, so this is the reliable join for it (the catalog
368	// does not expose a cell field, so slug — not cell name — is the only
369	// reliable join key; see cell_fanout.go's groupReposByCell for the same rule).
370	func matchClusterBySlug(clusters []coreapi.Cluster, clusterSlug string) (coreapi.Cluster, bool) {
371		want := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(clusterSlug))
372		if want == "" {
373			return coreapi.Cluster{}, false
374		}
375		for _, cl := range clusters {
376			if strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimSpace(cl.Slug), want) {
377				return cl, true
378			}
379		}
380		return coreapi.Cluster{}, false
381	}

14	// (the data API origin) carrying the matching login context's account access
15	// token (see auth.ResolveDataAPIToken).
16	//
17	// Pass insecureHTTP=true to allow plain HTTP base URLs for local
18	// development. Only the data origin is checked here — the bearer travels
19	// there on resource requests; the refresh leg is guarded by the per-context
20	// token manager (https required outside loopback/opt-in).
21	func NewAuthenticatedAPIClient(ctx context.Context, insecureHTTP bool) (*api.Client, error) {
22		dataURL := api.BaseURL()
23		if insecureHTTP {
24			auth.EnableInsecureHTTP()
25		} else if err := api.RequireSecureURL(dataURL); err != nil {
26			return nil, fmt.Errorf("base URL check: %w", err)
27		}
28	
29		// ResolveDataAPIToken discovers which login context the data host trusts
30		// (via its /.well-known/entire-api.json) and returns that context's
31		// refreshed login JWT. It normalises dataURL to an origin internally.
32		token, err := auth.ResolveDataAPIToken(ctx, dataURL)
33		if err != nil {
34			if errors.Is(err, auth.ErrNotLoggedIn) {
35				// Wrap the original err (not the sentinel) so any context
36				// the tokenmanager attached — keyring backend message,
37				// expired-token reason — survives to the caller. The
38				// errors.Is(err, auth.ErrNotLoggedIn) chain is preserved
39				// because err already wraps the sentinel; replacing it
40				// with the bare sentinel would drop that context for
41				// zero behavioural gain.
42				return nil, fmt.Errorf("not logged in (run 'entire login' first): %w", err)
43			}
44			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve API token: %w", err)
45		}
46	
47		return api.NewClient(token), nil
48	}

50	// NewAuthenticatedEntireAPICellClient creates an API client for repo-scoped
51	// entire-api routes (e.g. trails, experts). It exchanges the login JWT for a
52	// jurisdictional identity token and dials the entire-api cell directly, because
53	// the BFF does not proxy these routes for bearer callers (COR-666).
54	//
55	// fullName (owner/repo) or ulid identifies the repo whose cell to reach; ulid
56	// wins when both are set, and both being empty is an error, not a fallback to
57	// the caller's home cell. The repo's PROCESSING cell + jurisdiction are
58	// resolved from the control plane
59	// (mirroring the BFF's per-repo cell selection) so the call lands in the
60	// region that actually holds the repo's data. This is NOT best-effort: a
61	// resolution failure fails the command instead of falling back to the
62	// caller's home cell, because for repo-scoped data a silent wrong-region
63	// "success" is worse than an error — that fallback is exactly what used to
64	// make `entire trail`/`entire experts` read the wrong region for a
65	// multi-homed repo like entirehq/entire.io.
66	func NewAuthenticatedEntireAPICellClient(ctx context.Context, insecureHTTP bool, fullName, ulid string) (*api.Client, error) {
67		target, err := resolveRepoCellTarget(ctx, fullName, ulid)
68		if err != nil {

70		}
71		// NewEntireAPICellClient already returns user-facing, context-rich errors
72		// (login hint, discovery-unavailable, region guidance); re-wrapping here
73		// would bury them, so surface them verbatim.
74		return auth.NewEntireAPICellClient(ctx, insecureHTTP, target) //nolint:wrapcheck // pass through contextual auth errors
75	}

78	// package seam so tests can substitute a client pointed at a stub server.
79	var newTrailAPIClient = func(ctx context.Context, insecureHTTP bool, fullName string) (*api.Client, error) {
80		client, err := NewAuthenticatedEntireAPICellClient(ctx, insecureHTTP, fullName, "")
81		if errors.Is(err, clusterdiscovery.ErrNoAuthContext) {

84			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: %w", auth.ErrNotLoggedIn, err)
85		}
86		if err != nil {
87			return nil, err
88		}

## claude.ai entire-staging-eu
Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Reads are curated `*_entire` tools; a small write/ops group covers trail/review/runner/dispatch mutations.

Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

Querying conventions (shared by every tool):
- Addressing: name a repo by a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) or a repo ULID. Repo ULIDs are REGION-SCOPED — the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never carry a ULID across regions or sessions; if a tool rejects one, re-resolve with resolve_entire_repo.
- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".
- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).
- Size: reads that can be large (files, diffs, transcripts) honor max_tokens and return next_cursor to continue — raise max_tokens or page rather than assuming truncation is the whole story.

Pitfalls:
- sessions[].tokenUsage on a checkpoint is a PER-CHECKPOINT delta, not a session total — sum across a session's checkpoints, or use get_entire_session for the authoritative total.
- list_entire_checkpoints silently truncates older history; for a branch's COMPLETE checkpoint membership, paginate list_entire_commits and collect the per-commit checkpoint IDs.

## Summary

`entire experts --repo owner/repo` resolved its entire-api cell via `resolveRepoCellPlacement` (control plane), then discarded the placement id it got back and re-resolved the same repo's id with a second, redundant `GET /api/v1/repos` call, linear-scanning the caller's accessible-repo list for a `full_name` match.

`resolveRepoCellPlacement` already returns both halves from one lookup: `RepoID` (the processing placement id) and `Target` (the cell hosting it). This mirrors `explain --repo` (`explain_repo.go`), which already does this correctly.

**What now resolves the repo id:** for the owner/repo form, `resolveRepoCellPlacement(ctx, owner, repo)` — its `RepoID` and `Target` come from the same placement, so they can never point at different placements. The ULID form is unchanged: it still calls `resolveRepoCellTarget` directly and uses the ULID as the repo id.

**What was deleted:** `resolveExpertsRepoID`, `listExpertsAccessibleRepos`, `expertsRepoListItem`, and `expertsReposListPath` (the GET-based repo lookup). `expertsAPIClient` is now POST-only — the `Get` method is gone entirely, so a future regression back to a listing-based lookup would fail to compile rather than silently reappear.

**Test seam change:** `newExpertsAPIClient` / `setExpertsClientFactoryForTest` used to take `(fullName, ulid string)`; they now take a resolved `*auth.CellTarget`, since the repo id and the cell are resolved together before the client is built. Tests fake the control plane (`newCellCoreClient`, reusing `cell_target_test.go`'s `fakeCellCore`/`withFakeCellCore`/fixture helpers) to drive `resolveRepoCellPlacement`, and separately fake the entire-api client for the POST call.

**Error messages that change, and why:** a not-onboarded or failed/suspended repo used to surface `resolveExpertsRepoID`'s generic "may be homed in another Entire region, not onboarded, or outside your access" guess. It now goes through the same `errRepoNotOnboarded` / `renderRepoNotOnboarded` path the control-plane resolvers use everywhere else, which distinguishes "not onboarded" from "processing placement is failed/suspended" instead of guessing. This is also expected to fix an unreproduced bug: entire-api's `/repos` is the affiliation set (excludes repos the caller can read via public/broad access but doesn't belong to), so a public repo the caller could read might previously report "not found" even though the underlying experts POST route would have allowed it. Not verified in this change — flagging it as expected, not claimed.

This is the last known CLI caller of entire-api's `GET /repos` (COR-1370 tracks retiring the endpoint once older CLI versions age out).

Summary of the fix:

- Test seam (`newExpertsAPIClient`/`setExpertsClientFactoryForTest`) now takes a resolved `*auth.CellTarget` rather than `(fullName, ulid)`.
- Not-onboarded / failed-placement errors now go through the shared control-plane error path instead of the old three-guesses message.
- Verified: `mise run fmt && lint` clean, full unit suite (10333 tests) passes, integration suite passes except 3 pre-existing `TestPluginRemoteInstall_*` failures I confirmed also fail on a clean `main` checkout (unrelated git-tag environment issue), and the E2E Vogon/roger-roger canary (60 tests) passes.
